abstraction_design.rationale: The component and data-helper abstractions stretch well, but a Moves-shaped Items section would copy a handler and page with edits, adding sorting to card lists touches four pages, and the missing shared types layer means every new resource duplicates its shape twice.

findings.issue: Every page hand-declares an interface mirroring its server route's return shape (also moves/[name].vue:2-10, abilities/[name].vue:2-5, types/[name].vue:3-11, index.vue:2-6); nothing keeps them in sync
findings.suggestion: Move the response types (Card, TypeInfo, MoveRow-like payloads) into a shared/ folder and import them via the #shared alias in both server handlers and pages, per current Nuxt 4 practice

findings.issue: humanize is implemented twice with slightly different bodies (server vs app/utils/format.ts:3), so a display-name rule change (e.g. 'Mr Mime' vs 'Mr. Mime') is a two-place fix
findings.suggestion: Keep one implementation in shared/utils (via #shared) and use it in both the Nitro server and the Vue app

findings.issue: The 'N Pokémon' count + CardGrid + v-for PokemonCard block is duplicated in four pages, so any cross-cutting card-list behaviour (sorting, empty state, batching) is a four-file change
findings.suggestion: Extract a PokemonCardList component that owns the list, ordering and count, parameterised by the card array and optional per-card props

findings.issue: The typeRef mapping (`labels[t.name] ?? humanize(t.name)`) is repeated in three handlers
findings.suggestion: Add a typeRef(labels, name) helper next to typeLabels() in server/utils/pokeapi.ts

findings.issue: PokeAPI client and handlers are typed as `any` throughout, so refactoring a data shape or endpoint contract has no compile-time safety net
findings.suggestion: Give pokeapi a concrete generic or declared response type for the resources it fetches, at least for the fields the app reads

findings.issue: The app shell (SiteHeader/SiteFooter/container) is duplicated between app.vue and error.vue, with an `external` prop threaded through SiteHeader to make it work
findings.suggestion: Use a Nuxt layout (or a shared AppShell component) so error.vue gets the chrome for free

summary: This is a well-organized Nuxt 4 codebase: one server util owns the external API, one composable owns page fetching, and components are narrow and reusable, so most targeted fixes and source changes are one-file changes. The recurring costs are the absent shared types layer — every page re-declares its endpoint's shape by hand — and small duplications (humanize, the card-list block, the typeRef mapping) that turn cross-cutting changes into multi-file edits. Net: pleasant to own, with room to consolidate before it grows another resource section.
